```
#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without t
…[439 chars cut]…
-build.out 2>&1 || {

# A BINARY THE PROGRAM LAYER PLACES IS ITS KEPT BINARY, LINKED: a census compiler left from an earlier
# run can be that same file, which `mv` will not move onto itself — the old one goes first.
[ ! -e "$out" ] || find "$out" -delete
mv packages/cli/src/main "$out"
# A C symbol wears a leading underscore on macOS and none on Linux.
```

```
| **exact-count gate** | the census totals per cold workload, and the answers a warm run works out again after each fixed edit, over one pinned snapshot, against `tools/cost.baseline` | regressions: any counter that rose past tolerance, cold or warm | a gate slice (`make cost`); lowering a counter needs `make cost-accept` |

**The classifier** is what makes candidates automatic. A census site's SHAPE names its technique:

| site shape (from the census) | technique |
|---|---|
| a box freed in the fn that made it | stack records (escape analysis) |
| a free at rc 1 followed by an alloc of the same size | reuse in place |
| a retain whose release is the binding's last use | move at last use |
| `avra_streq`/name compare callers | interned names |
| a box of flat scalar fields pushed into a list | strided list |
| a slot box over a crossed box (`F?`) | nullable flat record |
| a list made and only walked once | deforestation |
| an indirect call whose target set is one fn | devirtualization |
| a `dyn` box laid with N code pointers | static method tables |

`avra census --candidates` prints the top sites per technique with their counts and the source
line, so a ranked work list is one command. Run per batch on the gate's workloads, its output
diffed against the last run is how a NEW candidate appears without anyone looking.

## How work is assessed

- **Every PR**: the exact-count gate holds; a new shape-rule finding fails like an idiom.
- **Every new feature**: its design post names its cost (boxes, calls, copies per use) and which
  registry rows it relies on or adds. A feature that makes idiomatic code slower needs a row that
  removes the cost, or it is not ready.
- **Maintenance**: a finding from any detector is a row or a ticket at discovery, never a comment.
- **New techniques** join this table with their detector in the same change.
```

```
# probe.sh <commit> [workload...]: the census compiler of <commit>, run cold over snapshot d5062c32

wt=/work/bis-wt
out=/tmp/claude-0/bis/$c
mkdir -p "$out"
[ -e "$wt/.git" ] || git -C /work/avra worktree add -f --detach "$wt" "$c" > /dev/null 2>&1
cd "$wt" || exit 2
git checkout -q -f --detach "$c" || exit 2
git clean -q -f -d -e build/ > /dev/null
mkdir -p build
[ -x "$out/avra.census" ] || {
    cp /work/b55-wt/build/avra-lane build/avra-lane
    make --no-print-directory $(make -pn 2> /dev/null | awk -F' := |= ' '/^PACKAGE_OBJS/{print $2; exit}') > "$out/objs.log" 2>&1
    s=$(date +%s)
    CENSUS_BUILDER=build/avra-lane sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$out/avra.census" > "$out/census.log" 2>&1 || { tail -5 "$out/census.log"; echo "probe $c: no census compiler"; exit 1; }
    echo "probe $c: census compiler $(($(date +%s) - s)) s"
}
src=/work/bis-src
cache=/work/bis-cache
if [ ! -d "$src/packages" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$src/build"
    git -C /work/avra archive d5062c32741cba87a5cb7964cb86e0a2768d5c1a | tar -x -C "$src"
fi
cp "$out/avra.census" "$src/build/avra"
find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name 'avra_hot.bc' -o -name 'avra_hot.inc' \) -exec cp {} "$src/build/" \;
for w in $ws; do
    case $w in
        check-program) cmd="check --counts packages/std-program" ;;
        check-cli) cmd="check --counts packages/cli" ;;
        build-cli) cmd="build packages/cli" ;;
    esac
    find "$src" -path '*/.avra-cache*' -delete
    find "$src/packages" \( -path '*/src/main' -o -name '*.av.ll' \) -type f -delete
    mkdir -p "$cache/home"; find "$cache" -mindepth 1 -delete; mkdir -p "$cache/home"
    sleep 3
    s=$(date +%s)
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    (cd "$src" && unset AVRA_MACHINE_STORE AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR && \
        HOME="$cache/home" AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \

done
```

```
    The exact-count gate: every counter of fixed workloads held to its row
    
    `make cost` (the `cost` gate slice; keepers-a1) builds the census compiler
    of the tree and runs it over one pinned commit of the sources: a cold cli
    check, a cold cli build and a cold std-program check, each census counter

    every run starts bare, and nothing is read inside the stamp window, so a
    check's counts repeat exactly. A row only falls, through `make
    cost-accept`; `COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> make cost-accept` moves the snapshot.
```

```
int64_t avra_enum_tag(void* box) {
    return box ? ((AvraArray*)box)->data[0] : -1;
}

// A tagged box's word, borrowed from it: 0 for a variant laid out with
// no payload slot, and for the null pointer.
int64_t avra_enum_word(void* box) {
    AvraArray* a = (AvraArray*)box;
    return a && a->len > 1 ? a->data[1] : 0;
}

// The same one level down: the box in a slot, made unique in place —
// avra_slot_unique's whole row, which its leaf hands every open but a
// unique box's in a box no log or guard must see.
__attribute__((noinline, cold))
void* avra_slot_opened(void* arr, int64_t i) {
    avra_box_touch(arr);
    void* p = (void*)(uintptr_t)avra_array_get(arr, i);
    if (!is_shared(p)) return p;
    if (box_is_static((Header*)arr - 1)) avra_wrote_static();
    AvraArray* a = (AvraArray*)arr;
    g_clone_site = AVRA_CALLER();
    void* c = box_clone(p);
    alias_log_clone(g_clone_site, c);
    g_clone_site = NULL;
    a->data[i] = (int64_t)(uintptr_t)c;
    mark_put(a, i, MARK_OWNED);
    avra_rc_release(p);
    return c;
}

// The same, for a slot whose word may be a scalar: only a slot that
// OWNS a box is opened; any other word is answered as it stands.
void* avra_owned_slot_unique(void* arr, int64_t i) {
    AvraArray* a = (AvraArray*)arr;
    int64_t w = avra_array_get(arr, i);
    if (!(avra_mark_at(a, i) & MARK_OWNED)) return (void*)(uintptr_t)w;
    return avra_slot_unique(arr, i);
}
```

```
// Shared means a count above one — the holder's own reference is
// the one. What is not a counted box is never one a place opens.
// AN IMMORTAL VALUE IS SHARED BY DEFINITION — nothing can hold the
// only reference to something that never dies, so a write through it
// must COPY. Without this an immortal box reads as UNIQUE and the
// write lands in the process-wide original.
static int is_shared(void* p) {
    Header* h = hdr(p);
    if (h == NULL) return 0;
    if (IS_IMMORTAL(avra_kind(h))) return 1;
    return avra_kind(h) >= 0 && h->rc > 1;
}

// AVRA_ALIAS_LOG: one stderr line per ACTUAL uniquify clone (never
// per call — is_shared already gates this branch to the rare case),
```

```
166 packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/backend/frame_census.av
//! THE FRAME CENSUS: which boxes a body mints could live in its own frame — a census build's label,
//! never a rule. A box is a candidate where a row mints it at a size known where it is made (a
//! constant `avra_array_sized`), and it stays one while every use in the body is a count, a read, a
//! write that fills it, or a hand-over to a seat that never keeps it. A store, an answer, a yield, a
//! pack, a `once` keep, a consuming row or a kept seat takes it out. What remains is labelled by WHY
//! it is eligible (a record, a list read in place, a list handed over), by the SOURCE of the
//! hand-over's lent fact (a runtime row's `keeps` column, or a user fn whose seats no analysis proves
//! lent yet), and by its size, with `single` where its one hand-over is all it is made for.
```

```
// Shared means a count above one — the holder's own reference is
// the one. What is not a counted box is never one a place opens.
// AN IMMORTAL VALUE IS SHARED BY DEFINITION — nothing can hold the
// only reference to something that never dies, so a write through it
// must COPY. Without this an immortal box reads as UNIQUE and the
// write lands in the process-wide original.
static int is_shared(void* p) {
    Header* h = hdr(p);
    if (h == NULL) return 0;
    if (IS_IMMORTAL(avra_kind(h))) return 1;
    return avra_kind(h) >= 0 && h->rc > 1;
}
```

```
void* avra_cell_unique(void* slot) {
    void* p = *(void**)slot;
    if (!is_shared(p)) return p;
    g_clone_site = AVRA_CALLER();
    void* c = box_clone(p);
    alias_log_clone(g_clone_site, c);
    g_clone_site = NULL;
    *(void**)slot = c;
    avra_rc_release(p);
    return c;
}

// Opens a mut cell's box only when it is the binary's own data: a
```

1. Cost of one open: 15.3 ns (open + push + release, C bench against libavra_runtime.a on 1 core, 37M iterations, 3 rounds). One box_alloc holds the header and 8 inline cells, and the mark bytes are zeroed. A fresh list sized for the push costs 11.7 ns. A fresh cap-0 list grown by its push costs 26.5 ns.
2. The open already is the lazy design: the immortal `[]` costs nothing until the first write, and that write makes exactly the one allocation a list born at its first push would make. No lowering can remove an allocation here. A list born empty and grown is worse (+11 ns).
3. Win ceiling: 3.6 ns (the is_shared → box_clone routing) × 37M = 0.13 s per cli build, about 0.07% of a ~200 s build. A runtime fast path in avra_cell_unique for the two static empties would remove most of it in about 5 lines, without touching the lowering.
4. The `empty_opens` row stays, so it ratchets, and the fresh-empty candidates still name sites where a list never needs to exist. Those are a deforestation question, which phase 2 covers.
5. Bundle 22752bc7 is unchanged (for batch 58). Phase 2 next: devirtualization (a census hook at each CallPtr) and deforestation (a walked-once label).</to_controller>

The frontier decides its cuts in place order, sorted by hash, a question's hash includes the code hash of the lowered code it reaches, and so any change to reachable compiler code reorders which question owns a shared read. That moves warm rows (they saw 280 vs 286 from an equivalent reorder). So part of batch 57's warm rise may be this artifact rather than real work. /// the names it keeps apart.
```
fn names_seen(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, space: Space) -> List<string> {
    let shared = module_bindings(engine, file.package_name, module_segments(file), true)
        .shared
        .names_in(space)
    let scope? = file_scope(engine, file) else { return shared }
    shared.concat(scope.own.names_in(space))
}

/// The names `file` binds at its top level, statement by statement.
fn top_level_defined(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> List<string> {
    let items = [read_item(engine, file, i) for i in 0..item_count(engine, file)]
    [n! for item in items for s in item.stmts for n in [item.store.let_name(s)] if n != null]
}
```

I've posted the per-row attribution for batch 57. I'm now measuring a fix for the main regression; the result is due in about 15 minutes.

**Where each rise comes from** (store pinned off, each merge measured with its own compiler, against cost56):
- **The measurement itself (defects, 2e56e49f).** The machine store is now on by default, and every cost run fills a store of its own. That alone accounts for about 6 points of build-cli's boxes (+16% → +10%) and about 3 points of check-cli's string_compares. Batch 57's `tools/cost.sh` doesn't pin the store off, and my batch-58 change doesn't either. Adding `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=0` there is the lead's call, since it changes the gate.
- **The real regression (parity-values 2f240144, commit 2aef1bec).** This is most of the rest:
  - build-cli boxes +8.1%, reclaims +8.4%, list_writes +8.6%, retains +6.3%, about the same on check-cli.
  - All the warm rises: body, comment and literal +13, signature +12, inline +9.
  - The cause: each item's law checks now call `top_level_defined`, which isn't a query and reads every item in the file. Cold, that is items-squared work. Warm, one edit re-works the law checks of all 14 items in the file instead of 1.
  - I checked this against the per-query breakdown of the warm runs. It is genuinely more work, not the hash-order effect parallel-main found.
- **defects, 4d873bb0** (the `// LICENSED` id check): string_compares +6.7% on check-cli and +4.0% on check-program. build-cli doesn't move.
- **laws-fusion, cd079c4a:** queries_computed +3.5%, and one new query (`item_instances_checked`) adds +1 to each warm edit.
- **Small or harmless:**
  - parity-types adds 0.3–0.9% spread over the cold rows.
  - lowering-quality touches build-cli only: boxes +1.2%, and string_compares falls 21.5%.
  - spec-harness is about zero, and the two gate.sh commits can't move a counter.

**The fix under test.** I marked `top_level_defined` as `@cut_query`, the same pattern `records_with_field` uses in that file. A file's top-level names are then worked out once, and an edit that doesn't change them stops there. It's a 3-line change in a scratch worktree, `/work/l57fix-wt`, and isn't committed. If the cost run shows the 2aef1bec rows returning to cost56 and warm law checks back to one answer per edit, I'll tell the lead the fix is confirmed. It's in parity-values' code, so it's the lead's to land.

```
workloads() {
```

```
// Whether this build counts the boxes runtime rows mint, by type:
// AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES set and not "0". The census's own build sets it.
int64_t avra_llvm_census_types(void) {
    const char* v = getenv("AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES");
    return v && *v && strcmp(v, "0") != 0;
}

static int stores_tracked(void) { return getenv("FORGE_TRACK_STORES") != NULL; }

// THE WAYS THIS PROCESS EMITS THAT ITS ENVIRONMENT CHOOSES, one bit each: frame pointers kept, boxes
// counted by type, stores tracked. Each makes another object of the same code, so an object's key
// holds them all (the build's `objects_salt`); read where each is read, so the key and the code agree.
int64_t avra_llvm_emit_modes(void) {
    return (int64_t)frame_pointers_wanted() | (avra_llvm_census_types() << 1) | ((int64_t)stores_tracked() << 2);
}

// becomes a private C string in `m`, read only by that counter.
void avra_llvm_build_census_box(LLVMBuilderRef b, LLVMModuleRef m, const char* label) {
    LLVMContextRef ctx = LLVMGetModuleContext(m);
    LLVMTypeRef ptr = LLVMPointerTypeInContext(ctx, 0);
    LLVMTypeRef fty = LLVMFunctionType(LLVMVoidTypeInContext(ctx), &ptr, 1, 0);
    LLVMValueRef fn = LLVMGetNamedFunction(m, "avra_census_box");
    if (!fn) fn = LLVMAddFunction(m, "avra_census_box", fty);
    LLVMValueRef text = LLVMBuildGlobalStringPtr(b, label, "census.box");
    LLVMBuildCall2(b, fty, fn, &text, 1, "");
}
```

```
        let found = flatten([candidates_in(read_text(p) catch "") for p in reports])
        for line in ranked(found, args.option("root")) { println(line) }
        0
    }
}
```

```
    let kinds = named_kinds(DSL_NOTATION, ["BREAK", "EOF"])

        lit_matches: (t: LexToken, text: string) -> t.text == text,
```

I have enough for both designs. Neither touches the grammar executor's source. The token_mask case is a third technique that changes how the executor is *compiled*, so that's the one to coordinate with laws-fusion.

<to_controller>phase-2 fix designs (not built; waiting for your go):
1. token_mask is not a one-target fn value. `Lexeme<T>` is a record of fn values. The executor's generic fns are specialized by LAYOUT, and the cli builds three Lexemes whose T is a box record: avrac's `Lexeme<Token>` (bridge.av:206), the DSL's `Lexeme<LexToken>` (std-grammar text.av:146) and std-sql's (parser.av:926). So one compiled token_mask serves all three, and statically its `wears_kind` has several targets. The census saw one only because the DSL and SQL lexers barely run. Fix C: specialize by TYPE wherever a generic body calls a fn field of a record over its type parameter. Then a program query (fn field → the values every construction of R<args> stores in it) makes Lexeme<Token>'s calls direct. This compiles the executor's lex-taking fns twice (Token and LexToken). The executor's source is unchanged, but its code size grows, so it's for you to coordinate with laws-fusion. 77M calls per check-cli.
2. Most other one-target sites are local. kinds_filed, first_typed, NamesRead.at, holds_stmt and closer_of all hand a lambda literal to `find`/`find_map`/`any`, which is lowered inline in the caller. The caller then reads the code pointer back out of the closure box it just made (slot 0 = `FnAddr(sym)`) and `CallPtr`s it; LLVM can't forward that through the opaque `avra_array_sized`. Fix A, row "a fn value the program proves has one target is a direct call": an IR rewrite before emission turns `CallPtr` on a slot-0 read of a closure box minted in the same body into `Call(sym, args)`, with the same ABI and the env still passed. It's local and sound because closure boxes are never rewritten. LLVM can then inline the lambda. The top-10 local sites add up to about 113M calls, and the census saw 255M one-target calls in a check-cli out of 497M through pointers. Later, the closure box itself becomes a frame candidate.
3. spans_of, literals_warned and misses_in all use `for e in [ExprId {…}]`, a one-element literal as a let. Fix B, row "a comprehension or literal walked once is never built": lowering `for x in [e1…en]` in a comprehension or `for` statement evaluates the elements in order into registers and runs the clause once per element, with no list (n = 1 is a plain binding). It's syntax-directed in avrac's comprehension lowering and needs no analysis. token_kind_of's `[…].first()` is a second shape, B2: stop at the first element. It changes behaviour if a later element has effects, so B2 only applies where the elements are effect-free; I'd leave it for later. walked-here totals 18.8M lists per check-cli, 2.2% of boxes.
4. Proposed order: A (largest, local, no coordination), then B, then C after you've coordinated with laws-fusion. Each lands with its registry row and its census delta as the receipt.</to_controller>

```
file_path: /work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/backend/direct_calls.av
--- content ---
//! THE DIRECT CALL: a call through the code of a fn box the body itself minted is a call of that code
//! (docs/ZERO_COST.md, devirtualization). A fn box is minted as `avra_array_sized`, its first push the
//! `FnAddr` of its code, its captures pushed after; a call reads slot 0 back and calls through it. The
//! target is read off the mint, never off a load: the box register must be the one the mint made, its
//! first push that `FnAddr`, each of the three defined once, and the box used in the body only as
//! pushes append to it, reads read it, a count moves on it, or a call hands it as its own box. Any
//! other use — a store, a pack, a hand-over to a fn or a row that may write it — and the call stays
//! through the pointer, so a closure stored, rebound or handed on is never taken for another.
use core.{Ins, Reg, dst_of, reads_of}
use features.{nothing}

/// The code each call through a pointer in `ins` is proven to reach, by its code register's index.
export fn known_callees(ins: List<Ins>) -> Map<string, string> {
    mut defs: Map<string, int> = {}
    for i in ins {
        let d? = dst_of(i) else { continue }
        defs.set(key(d), (defs.get(key(d)) ?? 0) + 1)
    }
    mut codes: Map<string, string> = {}
    mut zeros: Map<string, bool> = {}
    mut minted: Map<string, bool> = {}
    mut first_push: Map<string, string> = {}
    mut slot_zero: Map<string, string> = {}
    mut refused: Map<string, bool> = {}
    for i in ins {
        match i {
            .FnAddr(d, sym) -> codes.set(key(d), sym),
            .ConstInt(d, v) -> if v == 0 { zeros.set(key(d), true) },
            .CallRt(d, callee, args) -> {
                if callee == SIZED { minted.set(key(d), true) }
                if callee == READ && args.length == 2 && zeros.get(key(args[1])) == true { slot_zero.set(key(d), key(args[0])) }
            },
            .CallRtVoid(callee, args) -> {
                if callee == PUSH && args.length == 2 && first_push.get(key(args[0])) == null {
                    first_push.set(key(args[0]), key(args[1]))
                }
            },
            rest -> nothing(),
        }
        for r in reads_of(i) {
            if minted.get(key(r)) == true && !lets_stand(i, r) { refused.set(key(r), true) }
        }
    }
    mut known: Map<string, string> = {}
    for i in ins {
        let call? = pointer_call(i) else { continue }
        let box? = slot_zero.get(key(call.code)) else { continue }
        if call.args.is_empty() || key(call.args[0]) != box || refused.get(box) == true { continue }
        let code? = first_push.get(box) else { continue }
        let sym? = codes.get(code) else { continue }
        if [box, code, key(call.code)].all(defs.get(it) == 1) { known.set(key(call.code), sym) }
    }
    known
}

/// A call through a pointer: its code register and what it hands.
type PointerCall = { code: Reg, args: List<Reg> }

/// The call through a pointer `i` makes; absent for any other instruction.
fn pointer_call(i: Ins) -> PointerCall? {
    match i {
        .CallPtr(_, f, args) -> PointerCall { code: f, args: args },
        rest -> null,
    }
}

/// Whether the use `i` makes of the fn box `r` leaves its slot 0 as the mint made it, and keeps it in
/// the body: a push appending to it, a read of it, a count moved on it, or a call handing it as its
/// own box.
fn lets_stand(i: Ins, r: Reg) -> bool {
    match i {
        .CallRtVoid(callee, args) -> callee == PUSH && args[0].index == r.index && !args.drop(1).any(it.index == r.index),
        .CallRt(_, callee, args) -> callee == READ && args[0].index == r.index,
        .CallPtr(_, f, args) -> f.index != r.index && args[0].index == r.index && !args.drop(1).any(it.index == r.index),
        .Retain(_) or .Release(_) or .Cleanup(_) -> true,
        rest -> false,
    }
}

/// A register as the maps key it.
fn key(r: Reg) -> string { "${r.index}" }

/// The row that mints a fn box.
const SIZED: string = "avra_array_sized"

/// The row that appends to it: its code first, then its captures.
const PUSH: string = "avra_array_push"

/// The row that reads a slot of it.
const READ: string = "avra_array_get"
```

```
//! The lowering rule of a list comprehension: an empty list, then each head a walk inside the one
//! before, each filter a region around what follows it, and past the last clause the element pushed.
//! A head over a map walks its keys and its values side by side; one over octets, each octet.
use core.{

    Bound,
    CompClause,
    ExprId,
    Layout,
    ListWalk,
    Literal,
    Lowering,
    Lowers,
    OwnType,
    Reg,
    SignedType,
    literal_of,
    owned_type,
    rt_sig_of,
}
use core.expr.{Comp}

impl Lowers for Comp {
    /// A comprehension whose heads each walk a list, a map or octets, or count up to a bound. One over
    /// any other source isn't lowered yet.
    fn lowered(mut cx: Lowering, e: ExprId) -> Reg {
        let ty? = cx.type_at(e) else { return cx.untyped(e) }
        if ty.listed() == null { return cx.unlowered(e) }
        if self.clauses.any((c) -> !walkable(cx, c)) { return cx.missed_as(source_unwalked()) }
        let fill = filling(cx, self, ty)
        if fill != null { return filled(cx, ty, fill!) }
        cx.pack_declined(e, ty)
        let built = cx.list_made(ty, cx.const_int(0))
        walked(cx, self, 0, built)
        built
    }
}

/// A comprehension that is a fill: a count from `lo` up to `hi`, every cell the literal `cell`.
type Fill = { lo: ExprId, hi: ExprId, cell: Literal }

/// A count from `lo` up to `hi`, the bound read first.
fn counted_walk(mut cx: Lowering, lo: ExprId, hi: ExprId) -> ListWalk {

    cx.walk_count(cx.lower(lo), len)
```

```
//! a task it holds is joined where its scope ends. A named instance binds AND leaves its value, so a

        cx.gathered_into(j, self.value, r)
    }
}
```

```
//! The lowering rule of a list literal: one box sized for every plain element and every spread's
//! length, then each plain element pushed and each spread's slots appended, in written order. A list
//! the source alone spells is the binary's own data, read by its address, and an empty list of plain
//! scalars is the runtime's one empty packed list. A list of plain scalars is made packed. A `collect` is
//! an empty list, grown by each value its statements leave as they run.
use core.{ExprId, Lowering, Lowers, Reg, rt_sig_of}
use core.expr.{Collect, ListLit}

impl Lowers for ListLit {
    /// The elements first, then the size, then the box, then what fills it.
    fn lowered(mut cx: Lowering, e: ExprId) -> Reg {
        let ty? = cx.type_at(e) else { return cx.untyped(e) }
        cx.pack_declined(e, ty)
        if self.elems.is_empty() && cx.packs(ty) { return cx.call_row(cx.laid_out(ty), rt_sig_of("avra_array_empty_words")!, []) }
        let data = cx.static_literal(e)
        if data != null { return data! }
        let spread = [cx.store.spread_operand(k) != null for k in self.elems]
        let regs = [cx.lower(cx.store.spread_operand(k) ?? k) for k in self.elems]
        cx.listed(ty, regs, spread)
    }
}

impl Lowers for Collect {
    fn lowered(mut cx: Lowering, e: ExprId) -> Reg {
        let ty? = cx.type_at(e) else { return cx.unlowered(e) }
        let elem? = ty.listed() else { return cx.unlowered(e) }
        let built = cx.list_made(ty, cx.const_int(0))
        cx.gathering(built, elem, self.stmts)
        built
    }
}
```

### 2026-11-20T05:26:23 AGENT
Fix A is committed in its own worktree. Fix B is written but not yet built, and the 858c036f receipts are about two hours from done.

- **Fix A (904a7302, `/work/fixA-wt`):** a call through a closure the same function just created now goes straight to that closure's code. The target is read only from the instruction that created the closure, never from a load. Anything else keeps the pointer call: a closure stored, rebound, handed to another function, chosen by a branch, rebound in a loop, or declared at a different type. Its attack test, `features/closures/tests/direct_calls`, passes eval == native == expected. The registry row is updated.
- **8 closures spec failures:** when I ran the closures feature directory on its own, 8 spec cases failed. Plain 858c036f fails exactly the same 8 that way, so fix A didn't cause them. The gate runs closures together with the rest of its slice (avrac-b), and that slice passed. A's receipt will be avrac-b itself.
- **Fix B (uncommitted):** a comprehension head over a list literal of at most 4 elements, all of the list's own element type and none a spread, no longer builds the list. Each element is evaluated once, in written order, before the first turn, and then each turn binds the next one. Its test checks that order with side-effecting elements, including an inner literal that must never run on a turn the filter drops.
- **Fix C:** the compiler can already compile a generic function separately per type rather than per layout, for parameters with a bound. C extends that to a parameter whose body calls a function-valued field of a record over it, such as `lex.wears_kind`. A program-wide query will then show which functions that field ever holds.
- **A process slip:** while the receipts were running I created a file in their tree by mistake. I moved it out and restarted the receipts so they measure exactly 858c036f.

Once the receipts finish I'll bundle 858c036f, run the census delta for A, then build and test B and run its census delta. After that come the full receipts on the A+B head.

Lead: good root cause. But copy-aside and restore can't survive a SIGKILL or an OOM kill, which is exactly when a census run dies, and then the tree is left without its objects. The structural fix is that the census never builds in the tree's build/ at all: the counted runtime goes into its own directory (build/census/, with its own stamps), and the census binary links against that. Then nothing of the tree's is ever retired, and there's nothing to restore. # settle <stamp> <digest>: write the stamp when its digest moved, and retire its object.
```
settle() {
    old=""
    [ ! -f "$1" ] || IFS= read -r old < "$1" || :
    [ "$old" != "$2" ] || return 0
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$1")"
    printf '%s\n' "$2" > "$1.tmp"
    mv -f "$1.tmp" "$1"
    object="${1%.sha}.o"
    if [ -e "$object" ]; then find "$object" -delete; fi
}
```

```
#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
#
# NOTHING OF THE TREE'S build/ IS TOUCHED: the counted runtime stands in build/census/ under its own
# stamps (`make census-runtime`, whose goal settles no stamp of the tree's), and the builder runs
# from a copy of itself there, which links the runtime beside it. So a run killed at any point —
# signalled, out of memory — leaves every object of build/ as it was; the cli's own product goes.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
gone() { find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :; }
trap gone EXIT INT TERM
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
make --no-print-directory census-runtime > /dev/null
# THE BUILDER BESIDE THE COUNTED RUNTIME: a compiler links the runtime library next to itself.
cp "$builder" build/census/avra
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK: the old path's check the net runs first is not that work.
AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
    build/census/avra build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {
    tail -20 build/census-build.out; echo "census: the census compiler did not build"; exit 1; }
# A BINARY THE PROGRAM LAYER PLACES IS ITS KEPT BINARY, LINKED: a census compiler left from an earlier
# run can be that same file, which `mv` will not move onto itself — the old one goes first.
[ ! -e "$out" ] || find "$out" -delete
mv packages/cli/src/main "$out"
# A C symbol wears a leading underscore on macOS and none on Linux.
nm "$out" | grep -Eq '[ _]note_retain$' || { echo "census: $out carries no census — refusing to report"; exit 1; }
EOF
```

```
7987a3d3 held the tree's build/ aside and put it back, which no SIGKILL
or OOM kill lets run. Now nothing of the tree's is touched: \`make
census-runtime\` builds the runtime with -DAVRA_CENSUS into build/census/
under stamps of its own, and that goal settles no stamp of the tree's, so
no object of build/ is ever retired whatever the flags or environment.
The builder links it by name (AVRA_RUNTIME_LIBRARY, which a link keys by
digest like any library); a builder that reads no such name links the
shipping runtime, and the missing census symbol refuses the result.
Witnessed under AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1: two runs in a row both link, a run
killed -9 mid-make leaves the tree's build/ files hashing as before, and
the next run links.
```

```
the list. Witnessed with side-effecting elements (features/lists/tests/

first and once each, an inner head's literal runs per turn, and never
for a turn a filter drops.
```

### 2026-11-20T08:36:21 AGENT
The first census deltas exposed a flaw in how I was measuring fix A, not in the fix itself.

- **A measured as "no effect".** Indirect calls were unchanged: 497,438,896 on check-cli before and after. That wasn't because the fix failed. The compiler emits a direct call (I checked the LLVM output for a lambda passed to `find`). But the census counted every pointer call as it was emitted, including the ones it had just made direct, so the counter couldn't move.
- **A's own cost.** Its analysis added 0.85% boxes to build-cli, because it built its lookup maps for every function body. Most bodies have no pointer call at all.
- **B works.** Boxes fell 3.6% on build-cli and 3.9% on check-cli, list writes 1.3%, releases 1.1%.
- **The cost.sh fix holds at full scale.** I ran cost twice in a row on A+B: both runs linked and gave identical counts.

The follow-up is committed as 8a1d58cd. The census now counts only calls that still go through a pointer, and the analysis returns straight away for a body with no pointer call. A rebuild and one more cost run on this head are going, about 25 minutes. That run gives A's effect as the drop in indirect calls and B's as the drop in boxes. Comparing build-cli boxes with the previous A+B run shows how much of A's 0.85% cost the early exit removes. After that come the full receipts on this head, the bundle, and then fix C.

```
// One per 16 bytes of slab, reserved and filled by touch, as the births are.

    return r == MAP_FAILED ? NULL : (uint32_t*)r;
}

static void life_born(Header* h) {
    if (!g_scope_mode) return;
    if (g_birth_scope == NULL) { g_birth_scope = life_table(); g_box_rc = life_table(); }
    if (g_birth_scope == NULL || g_box_rc == NULL) { g_scope_mode = 0; return; }
    size_t i = (size_t)(((char*)h - g_slab_base) >> 4);
    int64_t d = g_scope_depth;
    g_birth_scope[i] = d > 0 && d <= SCOPE_DEPTH ? g_scope_stack[d - 1] : 1;
    g_box_rc[i] = 0;
    g_life_born_n++;
    g_life_born_b += (int64_t)(sizeof(Header) + h->len);
}

// Whether the scope `id` is open: the stack's ids rise from its bottom, so a halving finds it.
static int scope_open(uint32_t id) {
    int64_t lo = 0, hi = (g_scope_depth < SCOPE_DEPTH ? g_scope_depth : SCOPE_DEPTH) - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) {
        int64_t mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
        if (g_scope_stack[mid] == id) return 1;
        if (g_scope_stack[mid] < id) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

static void life_noted(Header* h, int64_t block, uint64_t born) {
    if (!g_scope_mode || g_birth_scope == NULL) return;
    size_t i = (size_t)(((char*)h - g_slab_base) >> 4);
    uint32_t id = g_birth_scope[i];
    if (id == 0) return;
    int64_t rc = g_box_rc[i];
    g_birth_scope[i] = 0;
    if (id == 1) { g_life_none_n++; g_life_none_b += block; g_life_none_rc += rc; return; }
    if (scope_open(id)) { g_life_in_n++; g_life_in_b += block; g_life_in_rc += rc; return; }
    g_life_out_n++; g_life_out_b += block; g_life_out_rc += rc;
    Site* s = site_in(g_escape_sites, &g_escape_slots, born ? g_mint_site_of[born & 0xFFFFFFFFu] : NULL);
    if (s) { s->made++; s->count += block; }
}

static void life_rc(void* box) {
    if (!g_scope_mode || g_box_rc == NULL || box == NULL) return;
    Header* h = (Header*)box - 1;

}
```

Measured for the compiler (cold check-cli and build-cli, each query's computation as the scope), about 90% of boxes and 89% of bytes die inside the query that made them. That clears your 80% bar. For an ordinary program (std-json's tests, each function call as the scope), it's only 44% of boxes and 37% of bytes. Box counts cover the slab-allocated boxes, 99.9% of all boxes made.

**(1) Boxes and bytes, in scope vs escaping**

| | check-cli | build-cli | std-json tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| boxes died in their scope | 90.3% | 89.9% | 44.3% |
| boxes escaped, died later | 5.9% | 5.1% | 55.7% |
| boxes born outside any query | 1.9% | 1.7% | 0% |
| boxes never freed | 1.9% | 3.3% | ~0% |
| bytes died in scope | 89.2% | 88.9% | 37.2% |

**(2) Top escape sites**
- **Compiler:** list clones inside the runtime (4.7M; the census can't name the caller here), syntax-arena spans (2 × 4.3M), saved-layout writes (1.4M), tape texts (1.4M), untaped expression variants, store segments, filled lists, relation-table cells and arena side columns. These are answers, tapes, store segments and table cells leaving the query that made them.
- **std-json:** the same list clones, then error infos, built `Text`, the old parser's scanned strings and numbers, and quoted JSON. These are values returned up the call chain.

**(3) Retains and releases:** in the compiler, 58.0% (check-cli) and 56.7% (build-cli) fall on boxes that die in scope. Escaping boxes take 20.0% and 16.0%. The rest, about 21–27%, is on never-freed boxes and boxes outside the slab, which the census doesn't follow. For std-json it's 25.7% in scope and 74.3% on escapers.

**Compile-time runs in a cold check-cli:** 2,709 evaluator runs took 18.9 s of 199.5 s CPU (9.5%). They allocated 10.9% of boxes (89.2M of 816.4M) and 10.2% of bytes (6.9 of 68.0 GB). This was measured under the census runtime, so treat the share as indicative.

**Reading it:**
- Per-query regions would remove the allocation and freeing cost for about 90% of the compiler's boxes. They would directly touch only about 57% of its retain and release traffic.
- Per-call regions wouldn't cross the bar for a program. A program would need coarser regions.
- Running compile-time code natively could save at most about a tenth of a cold check's CPU.

```
//! A METHOD CALL NAMING A FIELD THAT HOLDS A FN calls that fn: the subject, then the field read out of
//! it, then each argument, then the code read from the fn's box, handed the box and the arguments. A
//! field of that name answers before any method of it.
use core.{ExprId, FieldSeat, Lowering, Reg, SignedType}
use core.expr.{MethodCall}

/// The field `name` of the record `subject` is, when it holds a fn and isn't a `state` field.
fn fn_field_of(cx: Lowering, subject: SignedType, name: string) -> FieldSeat? {
    let field? = cx.fields_of(subject)?.find(it.name == name) else { return null }
    let ty? = field.ty else { return null }
    if ty.head is .Function && !ty.nullable() && !field.state { field } else { null }
}

/// The call `m` of the fn its subject's field holds, a `mut` seat handed the place it writes through.
/// One through a `const` or defaulted seat, or handed an argument by name, isn't lowered yet.
fn field_called(mut cx: Lowering, m: MethodCall, e: ExprId, subject: SignedType) -> Reg {
    let fields = cx.fields_of(subject)!
    let n = fields.find_index(it.name == m.name.of)!
    let f = fields[n].ty!
    if m.args.any((a) -> cx.store.arg_label(a) != null) { return cx.missed_as("a call through a fn field naming an argument") }
    let laid? = cx.seat_layouts(fields) else { return cx.missed_as("a call through a fn field of `${subject.spelled()}`") }
    let box = cx.field_read(cx.lower(m.subject), subject, laid, n)
    let args? = cx.value_seated(f, m.args) else { return cx.missed_as("a call through a fn field whose seat promises") }
    cx.called_code(cx.layout_at(e), cx.code_of(box), box, args, f)
}
```

The hook point is `field_called` in features/impls/field_calls.av. There the subject's static type is known, and in a fill-keyed unit it would be `Lexeme<Token>` rather than `Lexeme<T>`. The hard part is the proof's symbol: it must be exactly the `FnAddr` symbol a record literal's lowering puts in slot 0, for a named fn as well as a lambda. That needs the lead's ruling on its warm cost before I build it, so I'll post the design now:

<to_controller>fix C, design detail before building (it adds a program-wide query, which has a warm cost):
1. Split: a type parameter is keyed by its fill (ParameterLayout.fill, the mechanism bounds already use) when a seat's record type over it has a fn-typed field that names it. Lexeme<T>'s fields are all fn(T, …), so every lex-taking executor fn splits into Token and LexToken copies. That's a one-line extension of bounded_params (item_lowered.av:1160).
2. Proof: a per-item query of the fn values each record literal and `with` of the item stores, per (record type with its args, field), as lowering would name them. Plus one program-level union, a @cut_query. A body edit leaves the union equal, so it cuts off with no fan-out, and only field-call sites in split units read it.
3. Lowering: field_called (features/impls/field_calls.av) asks the union for (Lexeme<Token>, wears_kind). With exactly one fn, the code read becomes FnAddr(sym); the env box is still passed, so the ABI is unchanged. Fix A's pass gains one case: a CallPtr whose code register is an FnAddr is known. Same declared-type guard.
4. Risk: the symbol in the proof must be exactly the one a literal's lowering puts in slot 0, for a named fn as well as a lambda. I'd derive it from the same function the value lowering uses, never re-spell it. A mismatch means a wrong target, so the attack test covers two Lexemes of one layout with different fns, a `with` that rewrites a field, and a record built in a fn and passed on.
5. Receipt as laws-fusion asked: the --release cli size delta, indirect calls removed (77M target), findings cmp-identical, and a census plus warm rows showing no fan-out.

### 2026-11-20T12:33:10 AGENT
A serious design conflict, so I'm stopping before building C. A generic unit's lowering is a query keyed only by (file, name, parameters, settled seats), with no program in the key. That's what lets std's prebuilt answers be shared across programs. A program-wide union read inside a unit's lowering would bake one program's proof into a shared unit, which is exactly the unsoundness the lead ruled out.

<to_controller>fix C: a design conflict found before building; I need a ruling.
1. Generic units are lowered by a query keyed by (file, name, parameters, settled seats) with no program in it (item_lowered.av lowered_under/lowered_settled). That is what lets the prebuilt std answers be shared. So a program-wide union read inside token_mask$Token's lowering would bake one program's proof into a unit every program shares, which is the unsoundness you ruled out. Putting the proof into the unit's key doesn't help either: the caller computing the key is itself a shared unit, so the dependence climbs to the entry.
2. Option P, program-level devirtualization at the program's own link step: units stay shared and indirect, and the program's build rewrites the known CallPtr sites in its own copies. It's sound and keeps sharing, but it is a new LTO-like stage. Weeks, not days.
3. Option K, closed by visibility: the union over the packages that can name the fill. That's sound for every program when the fill type isn't exported. avrac's Token is exported, so it would not reach the 77M target. I'm skipping it.
4. Option S, const-seat specialization, the mechanism the compiler already has (lowered_settled, keyed by the settled value, so shareable and sound). If std-grammar's lex seats were `const`, a call handing a settled Lexeme lowers a unit settled on it, and inside it lex.wears_kind is a known fn, so the call is direct. It needs: (a) a record of named fns to settle as a compile-time value (bridge.av says it doesn't today); (b) `const` on the lex seats through the executor's recursion, a source change in laws-fusion's file; (c) avra_lexeme() as a const. It's general, with no program-wide query, but it changes the executor's signatures.
5. Recommendation: S if laws-fusion accepts `const` lex seats, since it's per-unit and needs no new stage. Otherwise P as its own project. I'm holding C until you rule.</to_controller>

### 2026-11-20T12:33:55 AGENT
Settled seats today carry only a `Literal` (`SettledSeat { at, value: Literal }`, and the key is digested from `literal_spelled`). Settled const values are a `MetaVal` tree with no fn leaf. So the design:

<to_controller>design (a): a record of named fns settling as a compile-time value.
1. What crosses: MetaVal gains `Fn(decl)`. When the evaluator's answer crosses, a fn box whose code is a declared fn's `$w` wrapper maps back to its declaration, as workspace_analysis.av:810 already does for wrappers. A lambda, a closure with captures, a generic fn, or any fn value naming no declaration refuses: "a fn value that names no declared fn doesn't settle". The fn leaf is checked against the field's declared fn type at settle time.
2. How it's spelled: SettledSeat.value widens from Literal to a settled tree (Literal | Record with fields in declaration order | Fn). The fn leaf is spelled by its declaration's package path and name, e.g. `fn:@std/avrac/src/grammar/bridge.av.token_wears_kind`, never by a lift number, an address or a program-local symbol. settled_symbol digests that spelling, so every program settling the same value gets the same unit symbol, and the unit stays shareable.
3. Lowering: inside a unit settled on such a seat, `lex.wears_kind(t, k)` (field_called on a settled subject) lowers to `Call(token_wears_kind)` with that fn's own seats, not even its `$w` wrapper, so it can inline. An edit to token_wears_kind's body changes what the call reaches, never the key, the same as any direct call.
4. Sharing: prebuilt std answers carry no such unit, because nothing in std settles a Lexeme. The cli's build lowers the Token units, keyed by avra_lexeme()'s settled value. A second program settling the same value reuses them.
5. Prerequisites outside (a): avra_lexeme() as a const, and `const` lex seats through the executor (laws-fusion's ruling). Holding until then.</to_controller>

→ [PWAtQUAR]
```
#!/bin/sh
# tool-witness: --self-test
# BUILDS A LADDER: each rung's tree, in a worktree of its own, with the compiler of the rung before it, and
# answers the last product's path. The one definition CI's prepare and a lane's Sprite both call.
#
#   sh tools/ladder.sh <compiler> <rung-commit>...      prints the last rung's compiler on stdout
#   sh tools/ladder.sh --clean <dir>                    removes a ladder's scratch (its caller does, once it has copied the product)
#   sh tools/ladder.sh --self-test
#
# A rung's compiler is a REAL generation (`make avra` run by the previous rung's product), so each
# step is the one the generation law already asks of a tree, and a compiler is never asked to read
# what only a newer one can. A rung that does not build names itself and its log; nothing falls back
# to the seed, which cannot read a rung either. The whole ladder is capped at AVRA_LADDER_S (900 s),
# each rung at what is left. A ladder that FAILS removes its own scratch; one that builds leaves it for
# its caller, who copies the product and then asks `--clean`, so no ladder outlives its use.
#
# A RUNG IS REPLAYED ON THE TREE UNDER BUILD, NEVER ON ITS OWN. With AVRA_LADDER_BASE set (the base the
# tree is judged against: origin/main for a pull request, the commit before for main's own push), the
# rung's tree is that base with the rung merged in — what a batch or a squash makes of it — so a rung
# whose branch began before the base moved is read with the base's sources, not its stale ones. A rung
# the base already holds is no rung: the starting compiler, built from the base, already reads it.
set -eu
# a compiler is replaced here by the build it just ran, so each build saves its store before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
# A ladder's scratch: each rung's worktree (registered in the repository) and its logs, all gone.
ladder_clean() {
    [ -d "$1" ] || return 0
    for w in "$1"/rung-*; do
        [ -d "$w" ] && git worktree remove --force "$w" >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
    done
```

### 2026-11-20T21:10:41 AGENT
Another scope finding that changes C's price. The executor stores `lex` inside `MatchContext` (executor.av:107), and the match recursion reads it through `cx.lex` 29 times. A const seat can't follow a value stored in a record field. So "const everywhere Lexeme<T> is threaded" means taking `lex` out of `MatchContext` and threading `const lex` as its own seat through every executor fn that takes `cx`. That's a refactor of laws-fusion's match recursion, on top of the new compiler path. Reporting before going further:

<to_controller>fix C: two scope findings; it's bigger than "a day". Your call before I go on.
1. The executor keeps the lexeme inside MatchContext (executor.av:107 `lex: Lexeme<T>`; `cx.lex` 29 times through the match recursion). A const seat can't flow through a record field, so a const lex everywhere means taking lex out of MatchContext and threading `const lex` as its own seat through every fn that takes cx: a refactor of laws-fusion's recursion, beyond adding `const` to signatures.
2. The compiler side is also more than the crossing. A const reaches lowering only as a scalar (const_literal) or as an evaluator-settled value (settled_const), and record consts always go through the evaluator, whose crossing turns fn boxes into plan-local ints. So it needs a new NamedValue for a const written as a record literal of named fns, read off the const's own syntax. Its read lays static data through the shared wrapper_symbol; SettledSeat gains the const's DeclaredName as the key, which settled_symbol spells, one derivation; field_called on such a seat becomes `Call(callee)`. Plus the three checks, kept to that same derivation so they can't admit what the layout can't lay.
3. Estimate: 2–3 days, mostly the executor refactor and its suites (std-grammar, std-sql, the bridge), plus the DSL/SQL lexemes as named fns over const kinds tables.
4. Value at stake: token_mask's 77M indirect calls per check-cli, plus the rest of the executor's lex calls. Probably 0.3–0.5 s of a ~60 s uncensused build, unmeasured. Fix A already removed 61M per check-cli at no source cost.
5. My recommendation: park C unless the owner wants the executor refactor for its own sake. If you say go, I'll do the compiler side first, behind a witness on a small program, before touching the executor.</to_controller>

Two findings for the gate work:
- **Builder cache:** gate.yml restores `gate-builder-${{ github.sha }}` with `restore-keys: gate-builder-`. That prefix fallback is what let any gate's builder be the newest cache from any run. The lead's fix replaces it with the landed head's exact key.
- **Generation:** a compiler records only its own print, a digest of its bytes. Nothing records which compiler built it, so a builder can't tell its generation today. The cheapest definition: `make avra` writes a provenance record beside the binary (`<tree sources hash> by <builder's record>`). cost.sh then refuses a census builder whose record doesn't show two generations on the current tree's sources hash.

```
# THE GATE ON A RUNNER: every slice `tools/gate.sh list` names, run from ONE seeded compiler, on a
# push to `gate/**`. The pushed branch is a one-commit mirror — the batch's tree over its parent, the
# trunk's — so the workflow is the pushed commit's own and nothing touches main; the idioms slices
# take that parent (HEAD~1) as the base their diff starts at.
#
#   seed    `sh tools/gate.sh seed`: HEAD's compiler, one generation, packed with its objects
#   slice   one job a slice: the pack unpacked, the slice run, its words kept where it fails
#   verdict one table: slice, PASS or FAIL, seconds
name: gate

on:
  push:
    branches: ["gate/**"]

concurrency:
  group: gate-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: read

env:
  LLVM_PREFIX: /usr/lib/llvm-22
  # a runner holds 16 GB and runs one slice; the old path's whole-package checks pass 6 GB
  AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB: "12000"
```

```
tested() {
    name=$1; shift
    pkg=$(echo "$1" | cut -d/ -f2)
    sh tools/bounded.sh "$ROW_SECS" build/avra test "$@" >"$out/$name.log" 2>&1
    ran=$?
    grep '^    ✗' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^    ✗ //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.failed"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.names" >"$out/$name.known"
    comm -23 "$out/$name.failed" "$out/$name.known" >"$out/$name.unpinned"
    grep '^avra: while running ' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^avra: while running //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.trapped"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.traps" >"$out/$name.traps"
    comm -23 "$out/$name.trapped" "$out/$name.traps" >"$out/$name.untrapped"
    if [ -s "$out/$name.untrapped" ]; then judged "$name" "$(wc -l <"$out/$name.untrapped" | tr -d ' ')"; return; fi
    # a run that fails no case and ends none must have exited clean; one that fails only pinned cases
    # or ends at a listed one stopped on them
    if [ ! -s "$out/$name.failed" ] && [ ! -s "$out/$name.trapped" ]; then judged "$name" "$ran"; return; fi
    judged "$name" "$(wc -l <"$out/$name.unpinned" | tr -d ' ')"
}
```

```
warm_edits() {
    warm settle
    cp "$src/$edited" "$out/edited.orig"
    edits | while IFS='|' read -r kind text becomes; do
        [ -z "$text" ] || python3 "$root/tools/cost_ratchet.py" --edit "$src/$edited" "$kind" "$text" "$becomes"
        warm "edit-$kind"
        if [ -n "$text" ]; then
            cp "$out/edited.orig" "$src/$edited"
            warm "back-$kind"
        fi
    done
    find "$out/settle.out" "$out"/back-*.out -delete
}
```

```
# A STORE IS ONE STORE WHICHEVER BUILD FILLED IT: the cli built cold in one mode, the product that
# mode must make; then that mode built over the store a build of the other mode left, that build
# working ahead on the cores or in one process alone (`AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF`), and the second build
# the other way about. Each product must be the cold one: an answer one mode's build saved is the
# answer the other's would work out. `modes-whole` ends each case whole, `modes-layered` layered,
# `modes` both.
asked_mode=${AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE-}
# The cli built as `$1` (whole or layered), alone in one process where `$2` is `alone`.
built_as() {
    case $1 in whole) AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release ;; layered) AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=dev ;; esac
    export AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE
    if [ "$2" = alone ]; then build env AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1; else build env; fi
}
# The cli's product as `$1` builds it, into `$2`.
product_as() { case $1 in whole) AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release ;; layered) AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=dev ;; esac; export AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE; unsigned "$2"; }
for m in whole layered; do
    if [ -n "${WITNESS_ONLY:-}" ] && ! printf ' %s ' "$WITNESS_ONLY" | grep -qE " (modes|modes-$m) "; then continue; fi
    cold
    built_as $m ahead
    product_as $m "$tmp/modes.$m"
    if [ $m = whole ]; then other=layered; else other=whole; fi
    for case in "alone ahead" "ahead alone"; do
        set -- $case
        cold
        built_as $other "$1"
        built_as $m "$2"
        product_as $m "$tmp/modes.after"
        cmp -s "$tmp/modes.after" "$tmp/modes.$m" || { echo "witness_program_edit: built $m ($2) over the store a $other build ($1) left, the product is not the cold one" >&2; exit 1; }
        echo "witness_program_edit: $m ($2) over a $other build's store ($1) — == cold"
    done
done
if [ -n "$asked_mode" ]; then AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=$asked_mode; export AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE; else unset AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE; fi
```
